BLOCKED on an enforced licence fee covering the instrument wording. iwasa_2016_asi holds the 16-item Anxiety Sensitivity Index (Reiss, Peterson, Gursky & McNally 1986), administered as the Japanese ASI-J. The ASI is fee-licensed by IDS Publishing Corporation: "The copyright to the ASI is owned by IDS Publishing Corporation and registered with the U.S. Copyright Office." (http://www.anxietysensitivityindex.com/), and its order form prices access as "ASI Downloadable Basic Order / Three-year license to download and print 2,500 Test Forms and 5 Manuals / $260/unit" (http://www.idspublishing.com/forms/ASI%20Downloadable%20Version%20Order%20Form.pdf, "Prices Valid Through December 31, 2026"). Enforcement is visible on the rights holder's own page, which serves the test forms only behind "Enter your access code to download ASI test forms" and restricts Qualified Users to "Licensed clinical psychologists, social workers, and counselors". Per references/itemtext_standard.md (fee-licensed instruments, ruled 2026-09-04 on the TAS-20) this is a determinate block and it applies even where the response deposit is openly licensed. No __items.csv written.

RETRY TEST: NO. Determinate on two independent grounds. (1) Rights: the fee licence is a standing term of the rights holder, unchanged by re-running anything today; it would change only if IDS Publishing released the ASI wording under permissive terms. (2) Availability: the administered wording is not in scope-recoverable material at all -- see the next note -- so even absent the rights bar this table could not ship the Japanese wording, only a translated substitute.

SOURCE GAP, independent of the rights block: the administered Japanese ASI-J wording is NOT in the deposit or the paper's own supplements. Checked all four PLOS Supporting Information files of 10.1371/journal.pone.0164630 (fetched 2026-09-07, cached under itemtext/.cache/iwasa_2016_asi/): S1 is the data workbook whose header row 1 carries bare codes only (id, sex, age, dpss01..dpss16, pi01..pi60, asi01..asi16, stai-t01..stai-t20) with no variable labels or item text; S2 is the Japanese DPSS-R-J questionnaire (16 items) and S3 its English version (16 items) -- both DPSS-R only, neither contains any ASI item; S4 is a JavaScript/analysis file. The paper body names the instrument and its anchors but reproduces no items. The ASI-J itself was published by Muranaka et al. (2001, 2002) in Japanese conference proceedings (Nihon Koudou Ryouhou Gakkai Taikai Ronbunshu 27:227-228 and 28:120-121), which are off-source and not open. So the only shippable text would have been canonical English ASI wording as a translated_substitute -- exactly the class the fee rule blocks.

Step 3b instrument check PASSED before the block: the table really is the ASI, not a mis-named sibling. The paper's Measures section states "The ASI is a 16-item measure ... ASI items are rated on 5-point Likert scale (from 0 'very little' to 4 'very much')" and "we used the Japanese version of ASI (ASI-J) ... consisted of 16-items and a single-factor structure identical to the original version". Live data matches exactly: 16 items asi01..asi16, resp set {0,1,2,3,4}, n=481 per item, 7696 rows. The three sibling tables from the same workbook are on different scales (DPSS-R 1-5, STAI-T 1-4), so the 0-4 range is discriminating rather than incidental. data/iwasa_2016_dpss_battery.py melts the source columns asi01..asi16 by name, so the IRW item code IS the source column name; had the table shipped, its code derivation would have been exemption-eligible.

Rights-holder statements consulted, for the audit trail: IDS Publishing product page http://www.idspublishing.com/asi.htm ("Qualified Users: Licensed clinical psychologists, social workers, and counselors"; "Pricing: Downloadable Version ... Paper-and-Pencil Version"); http://www.anxietysensitivityindex.com/ (copyright statement quoted above, plus the access-code gate); the priced order form PDF quoted above. A third-party distributor, the UW-Madison Addiction Research Center (https://arc.psych.wisc.edu/self-report/anxiety-sensitivity-index-asi/), states "We do not have copyright authority over these measures and cannot grant permission for use" and "Please contact the author of the questionnaire for use permissions. Please note: Due to the volume of requests, emails requesting permission for use will not receive a reply." -- corroborating that permission runs through the rights holder and is not obtainable by asking. Per the Shipley rule, no negotiation was opened.
